stage_a.note: They deliver the vision with a warm smile and an energetic, confident tone.
They demonstrate the snap feature of the glasses with engaged animation.
Kenzo playfully points to his dad, showing a friendly and approachable dynamic.

venture.description: Wearable reading glasses that securely snap onto the wrist for easy access.
venture.note: Kenzo states the product is reading glasses that change from wristwear to eyewear.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark and Kenzo introduce Eyewris, wearable reading glasses that snap onto the wrist, seeking 25k for 5 percent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if there are different sizes for the wristbands since she has a very small wrist.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban points out that the glasses only have little baby stems.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo explains it is a universal one-size-fits-all design intended to fit about 95 percent of the population.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks if they have a patent on the design.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark confirms they have a utility patent in the US, China, Japan, and soon in European countries.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the grippers leave a mark on the skin after wearing them for an hour.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark admits they might leave a little mark but says it has never been bothersome during continuous wear.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban notes that the reading glasses are not meant for long-term continuous use.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori agrees that they are meant for on-the-go use.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo confirms they are designed for the dozens of times a day one needs to quickly check something.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban asks what the glasses cost to make and what they sell them for.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo states they cost 30 dollars and 50 cents landed and sell for 110 dollars online.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks if Mark is an inventor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark explains it was a need-based invention because he constantly needed reading glasses but never had them with him.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Kenzo if he is an engineer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo confirms he has a bachelor's and master's degree in structural engineering from Cornell University.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Kenzo how he came up with the idea for the glasses.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo explains he applied the physics of skyscrapers to the glasses, prototyping the mechanism in his dad's woodshop.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara jokingly asks Mark what his reaction was when his son outwitted him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark laughs and remarks that starting a business with your kid is incredibly tough.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara notes they did not hear Mark's background and asks what it is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark shares he was a woodworker who started several companies, including bringing Gorilla Glue to the market.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara reacts in shock and admiration upon hearing about his involvement with Gorilla Glue.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if Mark sold his stake in that massive company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark confirms that he did sell it years ago.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the sale was a good outcome for him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark says it worked out very well and included a royalty component.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin excitedly asks Mark to confirm that he said he receives a royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark confirms to Kevin that he did indeed say royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how many units of the glasses they have sold so far.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo explains they did 28,000 dollars in sales during a testing phase, spending inefficiently on ads but turning a profit.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks how much of his own money Mark has put into the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark states he has invested about 630,000 dollars into the company.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin points out that since Mark has royalty income, he does not actually need their money.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond asks why they need a shark if they already have sufficient funding.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark explains his time is limited and he wants to leave Kenzo in the hands of successful, ethical partners.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara expresses deep affection for Mark's heartfelt explanation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban states he definitely wants to make them an offer because he is so impressed.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks Kevin to hold on while the other sharks notice she is getting emotional.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori tearfully explains how much Mark's desire to ensure his son's future touched her personally.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori offers 25,000 dollars for 10 percent, citing her extensive experience in the reading glasses market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark sincerely thanks Lori for her offer and kind words.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin offers 50,000 dollars for 10 percent, praising the product's simplicity and social media potential.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban emphasizes it is not about cash and asks the founders what they truly want from a partner.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo says they have the design and patents but lack the know-how to best distribute the product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asserts she has the exact know-how they need and asks who they would rather have as a mentor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark suggests they would prefer to have multiple sharks involved in the deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban says the leverage is theirs since all sharks love the deal and can help sell more.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark outlines their goals as expanding into retail, online sales, and licensing the technology.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond highlights his licensing expertise and offers to join Lori's deal, doubling whatever she offers.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori agrees she would be happy to partner with Daymond on the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark tells Lori that giving up 10 percent equity is too much for them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori clarifies that Mark's main concern is giving away too much equity for what the sharks bring.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if Mark would be willing to give up 10 percent if three sharks were involved.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban declares that he also wants to be included in the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara chimes in, stating she does not want to be left out of the deal either.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks what equity Mark would be willing to give up to have all five sharks on board.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark turns the question back, asking what percentage would work for all five sharks.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark Cuban explains how a five-shark deal works, with one doing due diligence and all contributing their skills.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin suggests the founders step into the hall to discuss it while the sharks confer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: In the hall, Kenzo asks Mark what percentage he is thinking, and Mark says no more than 15 percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: In the tank, Mark Cuban proposes they ask for 25 percent total, with each shark taking 5 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara points out that Mark never indicated he would entertain giving up 25 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin calls the founders back and tells them it is an unprecedented situation where all sharks want in.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Daymond presents a combined offer from all five sharks of 125,000 dollars for a 25 percent stake.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo counters the five-shark offer, asking if they would do the deal for 20 percent instead.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara immediately accepts the counteroffer on behalf of the sharks, saying they have a deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark happily confirms the acceptance, sealing the deal with all five sharks.

decisions.note: She knows the reading glasses market well and has the exact know-how they need.
It is a simple product to demonstrate and will work exceptionally well on social media.

decisions.terms: joins Lori's offer, doubling the investment and equity
decisions.note: Licensing is his field and he wants to partner with Lori on the deal.
All five sharks want to back them and combine their individual skill sets.
Wants to give up slightly less equity than the 25% requested by the panel.
Immediately agrees to the founders' counteroffer on behalf of all the sharks.
Happy to close the unprecedented deal with all five sharks.

record.notes: The pitch features a rare deal where all five sharks combine to make a single offer. An emotional moment occurs when Lori Greiner cries after hearing Mark Singer's heartfelt reasoning for wanting a shark.
